Precision-recall curve and AUPR for edge recovery

Source: R/eval.R
pr_auc.Rd

Computes the precision-recall (PR) curve of a score matrix against a true adjacency matrix, using the upper triangle. As in roc_auc(), the curve steps only at distinct score values (one point per block of tied scores), so the result does not depend on the order of the edges.

Usage

pr_auc(
  score_mat,
  truth_mat,
  method = c("trapezoid", "average_precision", "interpolated")
)

Arguments

score_mat

Numeric p x p matrix of edge scores (higher = more likely an edge), or a vector of edge scores.

truth_mat

p x p matrix of true edges (non-zero = edge), or a vector matching score_mat.

method

Summary of the curve: "trapezoid" (default), "average_precision" or "interpolated". See Details.

Value

A list with recall and precision (the curve, one point per distinct score, preceded by the point (0, 1)), thresholds (the score at each point; Inf for the first) and auc. If the truth has no edges or no non-edges, auc is NA.

Details

Three summaries of the curve are available:

"trapezoid"

Trapezoid rule over the curve points, starting from precision 1 at recall 0. This matches the tie-corrected compute_aupr() of the DiNA simulation. A straight line across a large tied block is not achievable in PR space, so this is optimistic for sparse estimators that tie many edges at 0.

"average_precision"

Step-wise average precision, \(\sum_b (R_b - R_{b-1}) P_b\) over tie blocks \(b\), as in scikit-learn. A tied block contributes at the precision of the whole block.

"interpolated"

Exact area under the curve obtained by interpolating true and false positives linearly within each tied block (Davis & Goadrich 2006; the continuous version, as in the PRROC package). This is the expected PR curve under random tie-breaking.

Without ties, "average_precision" and "interpolated" are close; with large tied blocks "trapezoid" can be much larger than both.

Edges with a missing score or truth are dropped.

References

Davis, J. & Goadrich, M. (2006). The relationship between precision-recall and ROC curves. Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 233-240.

See also

roc_auc()

Examples

truth <- matrix(0, 5, 5); truth[1, 2] <- truth[2, 3] <- 1
truth <- truth + t(truth)
score <- matrix(0, 5, 5); score[1, 2] <- 0.9; score[3, 4] <- 0.9
score <- score + t(score)
pr_auc(score, truth)$auc
#> [1] 0.55
pr_auc(score, truth, method = "average_precision")$auc
#> [1] 0.35
pr_auc(score, truth, method = "interpolated")$auc
#> [1] 0.3879424
